name: stations-r6
note: Stations round 6 (owner, 2026-10-24, from the in-game comparison): EVERY crafting station redone from its approved panel with two changes, the buildings' bright daylight (they came out dark, the Kitchen worst) and props scaled up to the buildings' absolute prop size (fewer, bigger). Two candidates each; the General Store is the light and scale reference.

mill-lit.prompt: REFERENCE: the first attached panel is this game's approved crafting station, the MILL: the timber stall with the sagging wheat-tan shingle lean-to, the flared pale windmill sails on the corner tower, the millstone, the sacks and the grain heap; the owner likes its design and layout: keep every piece where it is, the same camera, the same painterly rendering. LIGHT AND SCALE REFERENCE: the second attached panel is this game's GENERAL STORE, a building from the same village. Redraw the station with TWO changes only. (1) THE SAME BRIGHT DAYLIGHT AS THAT STORE: the station today is too DARK and dull; relight it in full, warm, high noon sun from high up and a little left, every sunlit face bright and saturated, the shadows short and soft and only in the recesses, the colours vibrant and cheerful, the whole piece as bright and sunny as the store beside it; no gloom, no heavy shading, no dark corners. (2) THE PROPS AT THE STORE'S SCALE: look at the crate and barrel by the store's door: that is the absolute size of a prop in this game. The station is only two tiles wide, so it holds FEWER, BIGGER pieces: every sack, pot, jar, basket, bottle and tool about the size of that crate, the machine filling most of its half and rising higher; drop the smallest props rather than shrink anything; the walls and posts stay the same height. PROP CAMERA: the third attached image is this game's barrel; every prop stays in that camera, front on and a little from above. Nothing else changes. The LAST attached image is a layout guide, a patch of the board grid with a tan 2 x 2 square: the station's walls, floor and pieces fill that 2 x 2 square entirely, back on its top edge, ground contact on its bottom edge, sides to its left and right edges (its tallest piece may rise above it), with a soft contact shadow to the lower right. Fill the surrounding squares with plain short grass in the same style, no props beyond those in the reference, and draw the faint grid lines as thin tile edges. Do not leave the tan square tan. No letters anywhere, no people, no animals, no smoke, no steam.
